- [LGRA.8.3.1] Disambiguation is **positional** — by grammatical position, not
  case ([LGRA.22]). In `type_ref binding`, the head — a bare `NAME` or a
  `lib.Schema` qualified reference — reduces to `type_ref`, and a
  trailing `NAME` reduces to `binding`. A pattern head is a type position, so
  every `.` in it separates a library path from the schema ([LGRA.22.4]).

  **A lone `NAME` clause is a pattern with no binding** ([LGRA.8.6]). The head
  stays separable on one token of lookahead: after the `NAME` that reduces to
  `type_ref`, a following `NAME` is the binding, a `.` continues the head, and
  `NEWLINE` / `within` / `where` ends the clause unbound. [LGRA.22.3]'s gate,
  table regeneration with zero conflicts, is what establishes it.
